himera.t: The first Greek city on Sicily's north coast, site of the great Greek victory over Carthage in 480 BCE and destroyed by Carthage in revenge in 409 BCE.
himera.o: Settlers from [[s:zancle|Zancle]], joined by exiles from [[s:syracuse|Syracuse]], founded Himera in 648 BCE at the mouth of the Himera river, on [[e:sicily|Sicily's]] northern coast. As the westernmost Greek city on that coast, it faced the Phoenician towns of [[s:panormus|Panormus]] and Soloeis and the Elymians.
himera.r: Himera spoke a mixture of Chalcidian and Doric Greek and was home to the poet Stesichorus. Its tyrant Terillus was expelled by [[e:theron-of-acragas|Theron of Acragas]] around 483 BCE and appealed to [[e:carthage|Carthage]]. In 480 BCE [[e:gelon|Gelon of Syracuse]] and Theron crushed the Carthaginian army of Hamilcar outside the city, and the Victory Temple was built in thanks. Theron's son then governed Himera, and later it was a democracy.
himera.e: In 409 BCE [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] Mago, grandson of Hamilcar, took Himera, razed it and is said to have executed 3,000 prisoners on the spot where his grandfather had died. Survivors and Carthaginian settlers founded Thermae Himeraeae nearby in 407 BCE. The ruins and battlefield cemeteries have been excavated.

hermione.t: Coastal city of the southern Argolid, known for its sanctuary of Demeter Chthonia and its purple dye.
hermione.o: Hermione lay on a peninsula at the southern tip of the Argolid, facing the islands of Hydra and Spetses. Greek tradition held that its first people were Dryopes, later joined by [[e:dorians|Dorians]] from [[s:argos|Argos]] in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]].
hermione.r: Hermione was a small independent city living from fishing, farming and the production of purple dye from [[e:tyrian-purple|murex]] shells. Its sanctuary of Demeter Chthonia had a festival with a famous [[e:cattle|cattle]] sacrifice, and a nearby chasm was believed to be a short route to the underworld. The city sent ships to Salamis in 480 BCE and was usually a member of the [[s:peloponnesian-league|Peloponnesian League]].
hermione.e: Hermione joined the [[s:achaean-league|Achaean League]] c. 229 BCE when its tyrant Xenon stepped down, and passed under Roman control in 146 BCE. The modern town of Ermioni occupies the site.
hermione.re: Greek religion; cult of Demeter Chthonia

hitu.t: A Muslim clove-trading state on the north coast of Ambon, whose long war with the Dutch East India Company ended in 1646.
hitu.o: Hitu was a federation of villages on the northern peninsula of Ambon Island, led by four chiefs called perdana. Its chronicle, the [[e:hikayat-tanah-hitu|Hikayat Tanah Hitu]] written by [[e:imam|Imam]] Rijali in the mid-17th century, traces its rulers to settlers from [[e:java|Java]] and the [[e:maluku-islands|Moluccas]]. Hitu's leaders accepted [[e:islam|Islam]] in the late 15th century through ties with Javanese ports and [[s:giri-kedaton|Giri Kedaton]].
hitu.r: Hitu grew rich selling [[e:cloves|cloves]] to Javanese and Malay merchants and kept close links with [[s:ternate-sultanate|Ternate]] and [[s:gowa-sultanate|Makassar]]. Its council of chiefs governed through village heads. In 1600 Hitu allied with the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] against the Portuguese, but soon resisted the Company's attempts to monopolise the clove trade.
hitu.e: The Hitu war, led by Kakiali until his murder in 1643, ended in 1646 when the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] took the mountain fortress of Kapahaha. Hitu's leaders were absorbed into the colonial village system, and the [[e:hikayat-tanah-hitu|Hikayat Tanah Hitu]] remains a key Malay source for Moluccan history.

hasmonean-kingdom.t: The Hasmonean Kingdom, the independent Jewish state founded by the Maccabees, whose victory is still celebrated at Hanukkah.
hasmonean-kingdom.o: In 167 BCE [[e:antiochus-iv-epiphanes|Antiochus IV]] of the [[s:seleucid-empire|Seleucid Empire]] banned Jewish practices, provoking a revolt led by the priest Mattathias and his sons, the Maccabees. Judas recaptured the Temple in 164 BCE. By 140 BCE his brother Simon had won full independence and was confirmed as high priest and ruler.
hasmonean-kingdom.r: Hasmonean rulers combined the high priesthood with political power, and from Aristobulus I took the title king. [[e:john-hyrcanus|John Hyrcanus]] conquered Idumaea and destroyed the Samaritan temple on [[e:mount-gerizim|Mount Gerizim]]; [[e:alexander-jannaeus|Alexander Jannaeus]] extended the realm across the [[s:hashemite-kingdom-of-jordan|Jordan]]. Pharisees, Sadducees and Essenes emerged in this era.
hasmonean-kingdom.e: Civil war between Hyrcanus II and Aristobulus II invited [[e:pompey|Pompey]] of the [[s:roman-republic|Roman Republic]], who took [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] in 63 BCE. [[e:antigonus-i-monophthalmus|Antigonus]] regained the throne with Parthian help in 40 BCE, but Herod captured Jerusalem in 37 BCE, founding the [[s:herodian-kingdom-of-judea|Herodian Kingdom of Judea]].

hsenwi-state.t: A powerful northern Shan state on the Burma-China frontier, at times a major Tai power, later split by the British into North and South Hsenwi.
hsenwi-state.o: Hsenwi, Shan Theinni, emerged as one of the principal Shan states of the northern plateau, with a ruling house that Shan tradition dates to the 13th or 14th century and links to [[s:mong-mao|Mong Mao]]. It controlled routes between the Irrawaddy valley and Yunnan.
hsenwi-state.r: Hsenwi's saophas ruled a large territory of Shan, Kachin, Palaung and Wa peoples, trading [[e:tea|tea]], [[e:cotton|cotton]] and [[e:silver|silver]] along the [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] to [[e:china|China]]. [[e:ming-empire|Ming China]] called it Muban and recognised its ruler as a pacification commissioner, while Burmese kings from Bayinnaung onward claimed overlordship. Succession disputes were common.
hsenwi-state.e: In the 1880s Hsenwi was torn by civil war among rival claimants to the saopha title. After the British annexation of [[e:upper-burma|Upper Burma]], the state was divided in 1888 into [[s:north-hsenwi|North Hsenwi]] and [[s:south-hsenwi|South Hsenwi]], which survived as separate Shan states until 1959.

helvetic-republic.t: France's centralised sister republic in Switzerland, which abolished the old cantons and subject lands and introduced equal citizenship.
helvetic-republic.o: French troops invaded the [[s:old-swiss-confederacy|Old Swiss Confederacy]] in early 1798, and Bern fell in March. On 12 April 1798 a constitution drafted by Peter Ochs of [[s:canton-of-basel|Basel]] proclaimed the Helvetic Republic, one and indivisible, with its first capital at Aarau.
helvetic-republic.r: The republic abolished the subject territories and created equal citizenship, freedom of religion and the press, and a single currency, the franc. Its directory and legislature replaced the old cantons with administrative units. Minister Philipp Albert Stapfer planned public schooling. But French requisitions, conscription and the suppression of resistance in Nidwalden made it unpopular, and the capital moved to [[s:canton-of-lucerne|Lucerne]] and then Bern.
helvetic-republic.e: Repeated coups and a federalist uprising in 1802 led [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] to impose the [[e:act-of-mediation|Act of Mediation]] in 1803, restoring cantons in a new [[s:swiss-confederation|Swiss Confederation]]. Its legacy includes the equality of cantons and the abolition of subject lands.

hong-kong-british.t: The British colony on the south China coast that grew from a small island trading post into one of the world's great financial centres before its return to China in 1997.
hong-kong-british.o: British forces occupied [[e:hong-kong|Hong Kong]] Island in January 1841 during the [[e:first-opium-war|First Opium War]], and the [[e:treaty-of-nanjing|Treaty of Nanking]] ceded it to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1842. Kowloon was added in 1860, and in 1898 the New Territories were leased for ninety-nine years, giving the colony its final shape within the [[s:british-empire|British Empire]].
hong-kong-british.r: A governor ruled with appointed councils, and the colony thrived as a free port and [[e:entrepot|entrepôt]] for the [[e:china|China]] trade. [[e:japan|Japan]] occupied it from 1941 to 1945. After 1949 refugees from mainland China fuelled a manufacturing boom, and from the 1970s [[e:hong-kong|Hong Kong]] became a major financial centre. Governor Murray MacLehose expanded housing and created the anti-corruption commission in 1974.
hong-kong-british.e: Because the New Territories lease expired in 1997, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:china|China]] signed the [[e:sino-british-joint-declaration|Joint Declaration]] in 1984. Governor Chris Patten introduced late electoral reforms, and on 1 July 1997 [[e:hong-kong|Hong Kong]] became a [[e:special-administrative-regions-of-china|Special Administrative Region]] of the [[s:peoples-republic-of-china|People's Republic of China]].

hikone-domain.t: The domain of the Ii family on Lake Biwa, pillars of the Tokugawa order whose head Ii Naosuke opened Japan to Western trade.
hikone-domain.o: [[e:ii-naomasa|Ii Naomasa]], one of [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu's]] most trusted generals and leader of the red-armoured troops, was given the former lands of Ishida Mitsunari at Sawayama after [[e:battle-of-sekigahara|Sekigahara]] in 1600. After his death in 1602 his sons built Hikone castle nearby, completed in 1622.
hikone-domain.r: The Ii, hereditary [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the Tokugawa with up to 350,000 koku, guarded the approach to [[e:kyoto|Kyoto]] and supplied several great elders (tairo) to the [[e:shogun|shogunate]]. [[e:ii-naosuke|Ii Naosuke]], tairo from 1858, signed the treaty with the [[s:united-states|United States]] without imperial approval and purged opponents in the Ansei purge.
hikone-domain.e: Naosuke was assassinated at the Sakurada Gate in 1860 and the domain was reduced. In 1868 Hikone switched to the imperial side. After abolition in 1871 it became part of Shiga Prefecture; Hikone castle is a national treasure.

habsburg-spain.t: The Spanish monarchy under the Habsburgs, the greatest power in 16th-century Europe and the age of the Spanish Golden Age.
habsburg-spain.o: In 1516 [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles I]], grandson of [[e:ferdinand-ii-of-aragon|Ferdinand II]] and Isabella I and of [[e:maximilian-i-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Maximilian I]], inherited the [[s:crown-of-castile|Crown of Castile]] and the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]]. Elected [[e:holy-roman-emperor|Holy Roman Emperor]] in 1519, he united [[e:spain|Spain]] with the [[e:low-countries|Low Countries]], Italian lands and the conquests of the [[s:spanish-empire|Spanish Empire]] in the [[e:americas|Americas]].
habsburg-spain.r: The monarchy was a composite of kingdoms, each with its own laws, governed through councils from [[e:madrid|Madrid]], the capital from 1561. American [[e:silver|silver]] financed wars against [[e:france|France]], the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] and Protestant powers. [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II]] built the Escorial, but faced the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] revolt and lost the [[e:spanish-armada|Armada]] of 1588. Cervantes, Velázquez and Lope de Vega defined the Golden Age.
habsburg-spain.e: Repeated [[e:sovereign-default|bankruptcies]], the revolts of 1640 and defeats such as [[e:battle-of-rocroi|Rocroi]] in 1643 marked decline. The childless [[e:charles-ii-of-spain|Charles II]] died in 1700, leaving the throne to [[e:philip-v-of-spain|Philip of Anjou]], which led to the [[e:war-of-the-spanish-succession|War of the Spanish Succession]] and [[s:bourbon-spain|Bourbon Spain]].

huexotzinco.t: A Nahua altepetl on the eastern slopes of Iztaccíhuatl that remained independent of the Aztecs and fought them in ritual 'flower wars'.
huexotzinco.o: Huexotzinco (modern Huejotzingo) was settled by Chichimec and Nahua groups in the Puebla valley in the 12th or 13th century, and grew into a powerful city-state that at times dominated neighbours such as [[s:tlaxcala|Tlaxcala]] and [[s:cholula|Cholula]].
huexotzinco.r: It was governed by a ruler (tlatoani) and nobles over a farming population in a well-watered valley. With [[s:tlaxcala|Tlaxcala]] and [[s:cholula|Cholula]] it formed an independent bloc east of the volcanoes, waging the ritualised xochiyaoyotl (flower wars) with the [[s:aztec-empire|Aztec Empire]], in which warriors sought captives for sacrifice. In the early 16th century it suffered defeats by Tlaxcala and sought Aztec help.
huexotzinco.e: Huexotzinco joined the Spanish against [[e:tenochtitlan|Tenochtitlan]] in 1519-21. Its nobles later sent a famous 1560 letter to [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II]] protesting excessive tribute. Its Franciscan monastery is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

heshun-confederation.t: Federation of Hakka Chinese gold-mining companies in West Borneo that governed its own territory for nearly 80 years.
heshun-confederation.o: From the mid 18th century Malay rulers such as the [[s:sambas-sultanate|Sambas Sultanate]] invited Chinese miners to work the gold fields of western [[e:borneo|Borneo]]. The miners organised themselves into kongsis, partnerships that held land and shares, and in 1776 fourteen kongsis around Monterado formed the Heshun federation, dominated by the Dagang kongsi.
heshun-confederation.r: The kongsis governed themselves through elected leaders and assemblies of shareholders, collected taxes, ran courts and schools, and kept armed forces. Their towns had temples, farms and markets, and they paid little more than nominal tribute to the Malay sultans. Rivalry with the [[s:lanfang-republic|Lanfang Republic]] and among member kongsis was frequent.
heshun-confederation.e: Expanding [[e:dutch|Dutch]] rule in the 19th century clashed with the kongsis over taxes and trade. In the Kongsi Wars of 1850 to 1854 Dutch forces defeated Heshun and dissolved the federation. Many Hakka communities in West Kalimantan descend from its miners.

hordaland.t: Petty kingdom around the fjords of modern Bergen, remembered in saga tradition for resisting Harald Fairhair's unification of Norway.
hordaland.o: Hordaland, the coast and fjords around what is now Bergen, was a populous district of western [[e:norway|Norway]] in the [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. The sagas describe it as a kingdom in the 9th century, ruled by local kings with fleets and many retainers.
hordaland.r: Its people farmed, fished and sailed; many western Norwegian raiders and settlers of the [[e:viking-age|Viking Age]] came from here. Hordaland belonged to the Gulating law province. According to Snorri, [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]] vowed not to cut his hair until he ruled all [[e:norway|Norway]] after Gyda, daughter of a Hordaland king, refused to marry a petty king.
hordaland.e: Its kings joined the coalition defeated by Harald at Hafrsfjord, traditionally around 872, and Hordaland became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]]. Bergen, founded in the 11th century, grew into medieval [[e:norway|Norway's]] chief town.

harhar.t: A Zagros town on the main road into Iran, captured by Sargon II in 716 BCE and refounded as the Assyrian provincial capital Kar-Sharrukin.
harhar.o: Harhar lay in the central [[e:zagros-mountains|Zagros]], probably in the Kermanshah region, at a key point on the route from [[e:mesopotamia|Mesopotamia]] to the [[e:iranian-plateau|Iranian plateau]]. It appears in Assyrian sources in the 8th century BCE as a fortified town ruled by local lords in the borderland where Median groups were settling.
harhar.r: Almost nothing is known of its own government. Assyrian texts say that the people of Harhar drove out a ruler installed by [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]] and turned to Dalta of [[s:ellipi|Ellipi]], prompting [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] to intervene. Its value lay in the trade in horses and goods moving along the road between the plateau and the lowlands.
harhar.e: In 716 BCE [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] took Harhar, settled deportees there and renamed it Kar-Sharrukin, 'Fort [[e:sargon-of-akkad|Sargon]]', as the capital of a new Assyrian province facing the [[e:medes|Medes]]. It remained an Assyrian outpost until Median expansion in the 7th century BCE.

hadejia-emirate.t: A north-eastern emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate, remembered for the rebel emir Buhari and for being one of the last emirates to fight the British.
hadejia-emirate.o: Hadejia arose from the [[e:jihad|jihad]] in the borderlands between [[s:hausa-kingdoms|Hausaland]] and the [[s:kanem-bornu-empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]], where [[e:fula|Fulani]] clans took control of the old [[e:hausa|Hausa]] town of Hadejia around 1808. Its first [[e:emir|emirs]] received their authority from [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]] and fought [[e:bornu|Bornu]], the Kanuri-speaking local populations and their neighbours in Katagum.
hadejia-emirate.r: Hadejia lay on the fertile floodplains of the Hadejia river, farming grain and raising [[e:cattle|cattle]]. The emir ruled through titled officials. Under [[e:emir|Emir]] Buhari, who reigned in 1848-1850 and again from 1851 to 1863, Hadejia rebelled against [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]], defeated punitive expeditions and raided its neighbours, before returning to allegiance after his death.
hadejia-emirate.e: Hadejia submitted to the British in 1903 but resisted their authority, and in 1906 British troops stormed the town; [[e:emir|Emir]] Muhammadu was killed. It then became part of [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Northern Nigeria]], and the Emir of Hadejia still reigns in Jigawa State.

hamidids.t: A Turkish beylik of the Lakes Region of south-western Anatolia, ruled from Egirdir, whose sale of lands helped the Ottomans expand.
hamidids.o: [[e:felek-al-din-dundar-bey|Felek al-Din Dundar Bey]], grandson of Hamid Bey, a [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] commander of the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]], established himself around Egirdir and Isparta at the beginning of the 14th century. A branch of the family took Antalya and became the [[s:teke|Teke]] [[e:beylik|beylik]].
hamidids.r: The Hamidids ruled the lake district around Egirdir, Isparta, Burdur and Uluborlu, a land of orchards and pastures on the routes between [[e:konya|Konya]] and the coast. Dundar Bey was executed in 1324 by the Ilkhanid governor Timurtash, but the family returned after he fell. The [[e:beylik|beylik]] built mosques and turned a Seljuk [[e:caravanserai|caravanserai]] in Egirdir into a [[e:madrasa|madrasa]].
hamidids.e: In 1374 [[e:kemal-al-din-husayn-bey|Kemal al-Din Husayn Bey]] sold several towns, including Beysehir and Aksehir, to the Ottoman sultan Murad I. [[e:bayezid-i|Bayezid I]] annexed the rest in 1391.

hephthalite-empire.t: The 'White Huns' who ruled Bactria and Sogdiana for a century, killed a Persian king in battle and forced Sasanian Persia to pay them tribute.
hephthalite-empire.o: The [[e:hephthalites|Hephthalites]] rose in the region of the upper [[e:oxus|Amu Darya]] and [[s:greco-bactrian-kingdom|Bactria]] in the mid-5th century, perhaps as a [[e:vassal|vassal]] people of the [[s:rouran-khaganate|Rouran]]. They drove out the [[s:kidarite-kingdom|Kidarite Kingdom]] and fought the [[e:sasanian-empire|Sasanians]], defeating and capturing Peroz I and then killing him in battle in 484.
hephthalite-empire.r: From their capital at Kunduz they ruled a loose empire from [[s:principality-of-samarkand|Sogdiana]] to the Tarim oases and the [[e:hindu-kush|Hindu Kush]], with Bactrian as the administrative language. Byzantine writer Procopius called them 'White [[e:huns|Huns]]' and described them as more settled than other Huns, with a single king and laws. They held Kavad I's Sasanian throne in their gift and collected tribute from [[e:persia|Persia]], and Sogdian cities prospered on trade.
hephthalite-empire.e: Between about 557 and 560 the [[e:first-turkic-khaganate|Turkic Khaganate]] under [[e:istami|Istämi]], allied with the Sasanian [[e:khosrow-i|Khosrow I]], crushed the [[e:hephthalites|Hephthalites]] near [[e:bukhara|Bukhara]]. Their lands were divided along the [[e:oxus|Amu Darya]], and Hephthalite principalities survived in Tokharistan under Turkic rule, later the [[s:yabghus-of-tokharistan|Yabghus of Tokharistan]].

hatay-state.t: A transitional state created from the Sanjak of Alexandretta in 1938, which joined Turkey within a year.
hatay-state.o: After elections held under Turkish military supervision gave Turks a majority, the assembly of the [[s:sanjak-of-alexandretta|Sanjak of Alexandretta]] proclaimed the State of Hatay in September 1938, with Antakya ([[s:principality-of-antioch|Antioch]]) as capital. [[e:france|France]], seeking Turkish support against [[e:germany|Germany]], accepted the change.
hatay-state.r: Tayfur Sokmen was elected head of state and [[e:abdurrahman-melek|Abdurrahman Melek]] prime minister. The state used a flag modelled on [[e:turkey|Turkey's]], adopted Turkish laws and currency and was closely tied to Ankara, functioning as a stage towards annexation rather than as an independent country.
hatay-state.e: On 29 June 1939 the assembly voted to join [[e:turkey|Turkey]], which formally annexed Hatay in July. Many [[e:armenians|Armenians]] and [[e:arabs|Arabs]] left for [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and [[s:lebanese-republic|Lebanon]], including the Armenians of Musa Dagh, who resettled at Anjar.

habsburg-monarchy.t: The composite realm of the Austrian Habsburgs, formed in 1526 when Austria was joined with Bohemia and Hungary, which grew into a great power on the Danube.
habsburg-monarchy.o: After King [[e:louis-ii-of-hungary|Louis II of Hungary]] and [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] died at Mohács in 1526, his brother-in-law Archduke Ferdinand of [[e:austria|Austria]] was elected king of both realms. This union of the [[s:archduchy-of-austria|Archduchy of Austria]] and the other hereditary lands with the Kingdom of [[e:bohemia|Bohemia]] and [[e:hungary|Hungary]] created the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburg Monarchy]], though most of Hungary lay under Ottoman rule for some 150 years.
habsburg-monarchy.r: There was no single state: each kingdom and duchy kept its own estates, laws and diets, bound together by the dynasty, the army and [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]], which was imposed after the Bohemian revolt was crushed at the [[e:battle-of-white-mountain|White Mountain]] in 1620. The [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] were driven from [[e:vienna|Vienna]] in 1683 and [[e:hungary|Hungary]] was reconquered by 1699. [[e:maria-theresa|Maria Theresa]] and [[e:joseph-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Joseph II]] centralised administration, taxation and schooling in the 18th century.
habsburg-monarchy.e: In answer to [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] imperial title, [[e:francis-ii|Francis II]] proclaimed the [[s:austrian-empire|Austrian Empire]] in 1804, giving the monarchy a single name and crown; two years later he dissolved the [[s:holy-roman-empire|Holy Roman Empire]]. The monarchy continued as [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] until 1918.

han-song.t: The Red Turban 'Song' dynasty of Han Lin'er, the millenarian rebel state under whose banner Zhu Yuanzhang rose to found the Ming.
han-song.o: Han Shantong, a [[e:white-lotus|White Lotus]] leader who preached the coming of the Buddha Maitreya and claimed descent from the [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] emperors, launched the [[e:red-turban-rebellion|Red Turban]] revolt against the [[s:yuan-dynasty|Yuan Dynasty]] in 1351 but was killed. In 1355 his general [[e:liu-futong|Liu Futong]] enthroned Han Shantong's son [[e:han-liner|Han Lin'er]] as emperor of a restored Song at [[s:bozhou-chiefdom|Bozhou]] in Anhui.
han-song.r: The state was a loose coalition of [[e:red-turban-rebellion|Red Turban]] armies rather than a settled government, inspired by Maitreya and Manichaean-influenced beliefs in a coming 'King of Light'. [[e:liu-futong|Liu Futong]] held real power and in 1358 took [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]], the old [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] capital, while other columns burned the Yuan summer capital Shangdu and raided into [[s:goryeo|Goryeo]]. [[e:hongwu-emperor|Zhu Yuanzhang]] at Nanjing was nominally one of its commanders.
han-song.e: Yuan forces retook [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]] in 1359, and in 1363 troops of [[e:zhang-shicheng|Zhang Shicheng]] killed [[e:liu-futong|Liu Futong]] at Anfeng. [[e:hongwu-emperor|Zhu Yuanzhang]] rescued [[e:han-liner|Han Lin'er]], who drowned in the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] in 1366 while being brought to Nanjing, probably on Zhu's orders. Zhu soon founded the [[s:ming-empire|Ming Empire]].

haushabi-sultanate.t: A small tribal sultanate on the road between Aden and Ta'izz, one of the British-protected states of the Aden hinterland.
haushabi-sultanate.o: The Haushabi tribe held the valleys north of the [[s:sultanate-of-lahej|Sultanate of Lahej]], on the main route from Aden into the Yemeni highlands. Its sultans, based at Musaymir, emerged as independent rulers in the 18th century as the [[s:qasimid-state|Qasimid State]] lost control of the south.
haushabi-sultanate.r: The sultanate was a small tribal territory with little central administration, living from farming and dues on caravans. Its position near the frontier with Ottoman, later imamic, [[s:republic-of-yemen|Yemen]] made it a concern for the British, who brought it into the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]] through treaties in the late 19th century. It joined the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]].
haushabi-sultanate.e: In 1967 the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took over the area, and the sultanate was abolished and incorporated into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

hungarian-state-1849.t: Independent Hungary proclaimed in Debrecen during the revolution of 1848 to 1849, which dethroned the Habsburgs and was crushed by Austrian and Russian armies.
hungarian-state-1849.o: [[e:hungary|Hungary's]] revolution of 1848 began with the April Laws, but by winter the court in [[e:vienna|Vienna]] was at war with the Hungarian government. After the spring campaign drove back Austrian forces, the Hungarian parliament, meeting in Debrecen, adopted the [[e:hungarian-declaration-of-independence|Declaration of Independence]] on 14 April 1849, deposing the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburg dynasty]] and electing [[e:lajos-kossuth|Lajos Kossuth]] governor-president.
hungarian-state-1849.r: The new state left the question of monarchy or republic undecided. Kossuth headed the state, Bertalan Szemere's government ran affairs, and the honvéd army under commanders such as [[e:artur-gorgei|Artúr Görgei]] recaptured Buda in May 1849. [[e:paper-money|Paper money]], the Kossuth notes, financed the war. Relations with Romanian, Serb and Croat minorities stayed hostile until a late nationalities law in July.
hungarian-state-1849.e: Russian intervention in June 1849 tipped the balance, and Görgei surrendered at Világos on 13 August. Thirteen generals were executed at Arad in October, and Kossuth went into exile. Neo-absolutist rule followed until the [[e:austro-hungarian-compromise-of-1867|Compromise of 1867]].

hunza-state.t: A Karakoram principality on the old route to Kashgar, once feared for its caravan raids, whose Mirs ruled from Baltit Fort until 1974.
hunza-state.o: The Mirs of [[s:zacazgo-of-hunza|Hunza]], of the Ayash dynasty, trace their line to a ruler who, by local tradition, divided the valley with his brother, the ancestor of the Mirs of [[s:nagar|Nagar]]. The register's start date is approximate. [[e:baltit-fort|Baltit Fort]], the royal seat, is several centuries old.
hunza-state.r: Hunza's Burushaski-speaking people farmed irrigated terraces and, until the late 19th century, raided caravans on the routes between [[s:kingdom-of-ladakh|Ladakh]] and Yarkand. The Mirs sent tribute to the Qing emperors of [[e:china|China]] while dealing with [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]]. Most people became [[e:ismailism|Ismaili]] Muslims. In 1891 a British force defeated [[s:zacazgo-of-hunza|Hunza]] and [[s:nagar|Nagar]]; Mir Safdar Ali Khan fled to China, and his half-brother [[e:muhammad-nazim-khan|Muhammad Nazim Khan]] was installed.
hunza-state.e: Mir Muhammad Jamal Khan acceded to [[s:islamic-republic-of-pakistan|Pakistan]] in 1947. The principality was abolished in 1974. The Karakoram Highway now runs through the valley, and [[e:baltit-fort|Baltit Fort]] is a museum.

habesh-eyalet.t: The Ottoman province on the Red Sea coasts of Eritrea, Sudan and Arabia, created to fight the Portuguese and control the trade of the Horn.
habesh-eyalet.o: After Portuguese fleets entered the [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]], the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] sent [[e:ozdemir-pasha|Ozdemir Pasha]], who in 1555 created the province of Habesh (Abyssinia) and in 1557 seized [[e:massawa|Massawa]] and the [[s:sultanate-of-dahlak|Dahlak]] islands from the Sultanate of Dahlak. He hoped to conquer the [[e:ethiopian-highlands|Ethiopian highlands]], and the province's seat moved between Massawa, Suakin and later Jeddah.
habesh-eyalet.r: The [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] held the coast, collecting customs from the [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] trade, and allied at times with [[s:medri-bahri|Medri Bahri]] against the Ethiopian emperors. Inland campaigns failed after [[e:sarsa-dengel|Sarsa Dengel's]] victories in the 1570s and 1580s. Day-to-day authority on the African coast passed to the Naibs of Arkiko, local Beja governors who ruled in the sultan's name.
habesh-eyalet.e: The province was much reduced over time, and in 1865 the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] transferred [[e:massawa|Massawa]] and Suakin to [[e:isma-il-pasha|Khedive Ismail's]] [[e:egypt|Egypt]]. The Italians later took Massawa in 1885, a step towards [[s:italian-eritrea|Italian Eritrea]].

hyderabad-state.t: The Nizam's dominions in the Deccan, the largest and richest princely state of India, ruled by the Asaf Jahi dynasty until Operation Polo in 1948.
hyderabad-state.o: Qamar-ud-din Khan, Nizam-ul-Mulk, the Mughal [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] of the [[e:deccan|Deccan]], defeated a rival at Shakar Kheda in 1724 and made himself effectively independent, while still nominally serving [[e:delhi|Delhi]]. Taking the title Asaf Jah, he founded a dynasty first based at Aurangabad; [[e:nizam-ali-khan|Nizam Ali Khan]] moved the capital to Hyderabad in 1763.
hyderabad-state.r: The Nizams allied with the [[e:east-india-company|East India Company]], accepting a subsidiary alliance in 1798 and later assigning Berar to the British. A Muslim, Urdu-speaking court governed a largely [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] population speaking Telugu, [[e:marathi|Marathi]] and Kannada. The state had its own currency, railways and postal service. [[e:mir-osman-ali-khan|Mir Osman Ali Khan]], reputed the richest man in the world, founded Osmania University in 1918 with [[e:urdu|Urdu]] as its medium.
hyderabad-state.e: [[e:mir-osman-ali-khan|Osman Ali Khan]] sought to stay independent in 1947. Amid Razakar violence and the Telangana peasant uprising, [[e:india|India]] invaded in September 1948 (Operation Polo) and annexed the state. Hyderabad State continued within India until it was divided on linguistic lines in 1956.

herodian-ethnarchy-of-judea.t: The short reign of Herod Archelaus over Judea, Samaria and Idumaea, whose failure led Rome to rule Judea directly through prefects.
herodian-ethnarchy-of-judea.o: [[e:herod-the-great|Herod the Great's]] will named Archelaus as heir to the kingship, but Augustus in 4 BCE gave him only the title ethnarch and the heartland of the kingdom: Judea with [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]], Samaria and Idumaea, about half of his father's territory, with the promise of a crown if he governed well.
herodian-ethnarchy-of-judea.r: His reign began with the killing of some three thousand people when he suppressed a Passover protest in the Temple courts, and further revolts had to be crushed by the Syrian governor Varus. Archelaus founded the village of Archelais, planted palms near Jericho and rebuilt the palace there. His marriage to Glaphyra, widow of his half-brother, offended religious opinion.
herodian-ethnarchy-of-judea.e: In 6 CE a joint delegation of Judeans and Samaritans complained to Augustus, who deposed Archelaus and exiled him to Vienne in Gaul. Judea became a Roman province under equestrian [[e:prefect|prefects]], and the [[e:census|census]] of Quirinius that followed provoked the revolt of Judas of [[e:galilee|Galilee]].

hirpini.t: Samnite people of the southern Apennines, named after the wolf that legend says led them, who resisted Rome until the Social War.
hirpini.o: The Hirpini lived in the mountains of modern Irpinia, east of Campania. Their name was explained from the Oscan word hirpus, 'wolf', after the animal that guided their ancestors in a 'sacred spring' migration from the Sabine lands. They were one of the peoples of the [[s:samnite-league|Samnite League]].
hirpini.r: Their centres included Maleventum (later Beneventum), Aeclanum, Compsa and Abellinum. They lived from herding and farming in upland valleys, and the sanctuary of the goddess Mefitis in the Ansanto valley, by sulphurous springs, was a major cult site. As part of [[s:samnite-league|Samnium]] they fought [[e:rome|Rome]] in the [[e:samnite-wars|Samnite Wars]].
hirpini.e: After the Samnite defeat [[e:rome|Rome]] founded Beneventum on Hirpine land in 268 BCE. The Hirpini went over to [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] after [[e:battle-of-cannae|Cannae]] and were punished. They joined the Italian revolt in 91 BCE; Sulla took Aeclanum in 89 BCE, after which they submitted and received citizenship.

habsburg-netherlands.t: The Low Countries under Maximilian, Philip the Handsome and Charles V, gathered into the Seventeen Provinces and bound to the Habsburg world empire.
habsburg-netherlands.o: [[e:mary-of-burgundy|Mary of Burgundy's]] death in 1482 left the [[s:burgundian-state|Burgundian State]]'s northern lands to her infant son [[e:philip-the-handsome|Philip the Handsome]], with her widower [[e:maximilian-i-holy-roman-emperor|Maximilian of Austria]] as regent. Maximilian fought rebellious Flemish towns and [[e:france|France]] for a decade before Philip came of age in 1494.
habsburg-netherlands.r: [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]], born at Ghent in 1500, rounded off the territories by taking Frisia, [[s:lordship-of-utrecht|Utrecht]], [[s:lordship-of-overijssel|Overijssel]], Groningen and [[s:duchy-of-guelders|Guelders]], forming the Seventeen Provinces. Regents Margaret of [[e:austria|Austria]] and Mary of [[e:hungary|Hungary]] governed from [[s:lordship-of-mechelen|Mechelen]] and Brussels with the [[e:states-general-of-the-netherlands|States General]] and collateral councils. [[e:antwerp|Antwerp]] became [[e:europe|Europe's]] main market, and Erasmus worked in [[s:county-of-louvain|Leuven]]. The Pragmatic Sanction of 1549 made the provinces one indivisible inheritance.
habsburg-netherlands.e: [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] abdicated in Brussels in 1555, handing the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] to his son [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II]]. Philip's rule from [[e:spain|Spain]] began the [[s:spanish-netherlands|Spanish Netherlands]], and his religious and fiscal policies provoked the [[e:dutch-revolt|Dutch Revolt]].

high-kingship-of-ireland.t: The prestigious title of king of Tara and over-king of Ireland, contested for centuries by the Ui Neill and later by provincial dynasties such as Brian Boru's.
high-kingship-of-ireland.o: The kingship of Tara, an ancient royal site in [[s:kingdom-of-mide|Meath]], was claimed from the 6th century by the [[e:ui-neill|Ui Neill]] dynasties, who presented it as an ancient kingship of all Ireland. Their northern and southern branches alternated the title for several centuries, though actual authority rarely reached beyond the northern half of the island.
high-kingship-of-ireland.r: The high king was an overlord rather than a ruler of a centralised state: he took hostages and tribute from provincial kings and held the Feis Temro and fairs. Monastic chroniclers and law tracts built up the ideology of a [[e:sacred-kingship|sacred kingship]]. Real power depended on military success.
high-kingship-of-ireland.e: [[e:brian-boru|Brian Boru]] of [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]] broke the [[e:ui-neill|Ui Neill]] monopoly around 1002, and later kings ruled 'with opposition'. [[e:ruaidri-ua-conchobair|Ruaidri Ua Conchobair]], the last high king, accepted [[e:henry-ii-of-england|Henry II]]'s overlordship in the [[e:treaty-of-windsor-1175|Treaty of Windsor]] of 1175, after the Norman invasion and the creation of the [[s:lordship-of-ireland|Lordship of Ireland]]; he died in 1198.

hiraab-imamate.t: A Somali clan state that rose on the ruins of the Ajuran Sultanate and dominated Mogadishu and the central Somali coast for nearly two centuries.
hiraab-imamate.o: In the late 17th century the Hiraab clans of the Hawiye, among them the Abgaal and Habar Gidir, revolted against the [[s:ajuran-sultanate|Ajuran Sultanate]]. The Hiraab established an [[e:imamate|imamate]], with the [[e:imam|imam]] drawn from the Abgaal and military leadership from allied lineages, taking control of [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]] and the coast north of it.
hiraab-imamate.r: The [[e:imamate|imamate]] was a clan confederation rather than a bureaucratic state. The [[e:imam|imam]] held religious and political authority, mediated disputes under [[e:somalis|Somali]] customary law and Islamic law, and drew revenues from the coastal trade in livestock, grain and [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]]. [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]] itself was split between rival quarters, Shingani and [[e:hamar-weyne|Hamar Weyne]].
hiraab-imamate.e: The [[e:imamate|imamate]] weakened in the 19th century as the [[s:sultanate-of-the-geledi|Sultanate of the Geledi]] rose inland and the [[s:sultanate-of-zanzibar|Sultanate of Zanzibar]] asserted authority over [[s:sultanate-of-mogadishu|Mogadishu]] in the 1870s. The area later became part of [[s:italian-somaliland|Italian Somaliland]].

hungarian-democratic-republic.t: Hungary's first republic, born of the Aster Revolution of 1918, which collapsed under the pressure of defeat and territorial losses.
hungarian-democratic-republic.o: As [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] collapsed at the end of the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], the Aster Revolution in [[e:budapest|Budapest]] on 31 October 1918 brought Count Mihály Károlyi to power as prime minister; on the same day former premier [[e:istvan-tisza|István Tisza]] was murdered. On 16 November 1918 the National Council proclaimed [[e:hungary|Hungary]] a republic, ending the [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1867-1918|Kingdom of Hungary]] (1867-1918).
hungarian-democratic-republic.r: Károlyi's coalition of liberals, radicals and Social Democrats introduced universal suffrage and began land reform, distributing his own estate. But it faced economic chaos, returning soldiers and the advance of Czechoslovak, Romanian and Serbian troops beyond the [[e:belgrade|Belgrade]] [[e:armistice-of-11-november-1918|armistice]] lines. Károlyi became provisional president in January 1919, with [[e:denes-berinkey|Dénes Berinkey]] as prime minister.
hungarian-democratic-republic.e: In March 1919 the [[e:allies|Allies]]' Vix Note demanded a further Hungarian withdrawal in the east. Károlyi's government resigned, and the Social Democrats united with the Communists, who proclaimed the [[s:hungarian-soviet-republic|Hungarian Soviet Republic]] on 21 March 1919.

hamath.t: Hamath, a Syrian kingdom on the Orontes whose kings led resistance to Assyria at Qarqar and left both Luwian and Aramaic inscriptions.
hamath.o: Hamath, modern Hama, rose after the [[e:late-bronze-age-collapse|Late Bronze Age collapse]] as a kingdom on the middle Orontes. Its early rulers wrote in Luwian hieroglyphs; carved stones from the city, noticed by Johann Ludwig Burckhardt in 1812, were the first Hittite hieroglyphs known to modern scholars.
hamath.r: Under King Urhilina, Hamath joined [[s:aram-damascus|Aram-Damascus]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Kingdom of Israel]] to fight [[e:shalmaneser-iii|Shalmaneser III]] at Qarqar in 853 BCE. Around 800 BCE the usurper [[e:zakkur|Zakkur]] ruled Hamath and [[s:luash|Lu'ash]], and his [[e:aramaic|Aramaic]] stele tells how the god Baalshamin saved him from a siege by a coalition led by Aram-[[e:damascus|Damascus]].
hamath.e: Hamath became a tributary of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]]. In 720 BCE Yau-bidi led a revolt; [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] defeated him at Qarqar, flayed him, and annexed Hamath as a province, deporting many of its people.

hungarian-peoples-republic.t: Communist Hungary, from Rákosi's Stalinism and the crushed revolution of 1956 to János Kádár's relatively relaxed 'goulash communism'.
hungarian-peoples-republic.o: After the communists eliminated their rivals in the [[s:second-hungarian-republic|Second Hungarian Republic]], a Soviet-style constitution proclaimed the [[s:hungarian-democratic-republic|Hungarian People's Republic]] on 20 August 1949. [[e:matyas-rakosi|Mátyás Rákosi]], leader of the Hungarian Working People's Party, ruled as a Stalinist dictator, with show trials such as that of László Rajk and a feared secret police, the ÁVH.
hungarian-peoples-republic.r: After Stalin's death [[e:imre-nagy|Imre Nagy]] eased repression, and on 23 October 1956 a popular revolution brought him back to power and declared neutrality. Soviet forces crushed it in November, and [[e:janos-kadar|János Kádár]] ruled for over thirty years. After harsh reprisals, Kádár allowed a mixed economy under the [[e:new-economic-mechanism|New Economic Mechanism]] of 1968, making [[e:hungary|Hungary]] the most liberal state in the Soviet bloc.
hungarian-peoples-republic.e: Economic problems and reformers in the party removed Kádár in 1988. In 1989 [[e:hungarian-round-table-talks|Round Table]] talks agreed free elections, [[e:imre-nagy|Imre Nagy]] was solemnly reburied, and the border with [[e:austria|Austria]] was opened. On 23 October 1989 the [[s:hungary|Republic of Hungary]] was proclaimed.

hanthawaddy-kingdom.t: The Mon kingdom of Lower Myanmar, centred on Martaban and later Pegu, that grew rich on Indian Ocean trade and held off Ava for over a century.
hanthawaddy-kingdom.o: After the fall of the [[s:pagan-kingdom|Pagan Kingdom]], Wareru, a Mon adventurer said to have been a merchant, seized Martaban in 1287 and gained recognition from [[s:sukhothai-kingdom|Sukhothai]]. His dynasty united the Mon-speaking coast of Ramannadesa, and in 1369 King Binnya U moved the capital to Pegu, also called Hanthawaddy.
hanthawaddy-kingdom.r: The kingdom's ports, Martaban, Pegu, Bassein and [[s:portuguese-syriam|Syriam]], exported [[e:rice|rice]], lac, rubies and the famous Martaban jars across the [[e:bay-of-bengal|Bay of Bengal]]. Razadarit fought the [[e:forty-years-war|Forty Years' War]] with the [[s:ava-kingdom|Ava Kingdom]] from 1385 to 1424 and kept Hanthawaddy independent. Queen Shin Sawbu and her successor Dhammazedi, a former monk, presided over a golden age; Dhammazedi reformed the Buddhist order through the Kalyani inscriptions.
hanthawaddy-kingdom.e: Internal decline left Hanthawaddy open to the rising [[s:first-toungoo-empire|First Toungoo Empire]], whose king Tabinshwehti took Pegu in 1539 and Martaban in 1541, making Pegu his own capital. Mon resistance revived in the [[s:restored-hanthawaddy-kingdom|Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom]] of the 18th century.
